title: The US House Just Voted to End the Iran War. Four Republicans Made It Happen.
excerpt: The 215-208 vote is the clearest Congressional rebuke of Trump's three-month-old conflict, but the measure still faces a Senate gauntlet and a certain veto.
body:
The Republican-led US House of Representatives passed a war powers resolution on Wednesday directing President Donald Trump to withdraw American forces from Iran, in the strongest Congressional challenge yet to a conflict that has roiled global energy markets and sent Indian fuel prices surging.

The vote was 215 to 208. Four Republicans — Tom Barrett of Michigan, Warren Davidson of Ohio, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania and Thomas Massie of Kentucky — broke with their party to join every Democrat present in favour of the measure.

## A Long Road to This Vote

This was the fourth attempt. Three previous war powers resolutions had failed in the House by increasingly slim margins. House Speaker Mike Johnson had postponed a vote on this version two weeks ago when it became clear enough Republicans would defect. The extended recess did not change the math.

"The passage of this WPR today signals a significant turning point: more and more Republicans are listening to their constituents who do not want another open-ended war in the Middle East," said Representative Gregory Meeks, who introduced the resolution and serves as the ranking member on the Foreign Affairs Committee.

The White House dismissed the vote. A spokesperson said the resolution "will not reach" the President's desk, pointing to the Republican-controlled Senate where a similar measure has advanced procedurally but has not yet received a final vote.

## The India Connection

One notable absence from the vote was Representative Pramila Jayapal of Washington, the Indian-American lawmaker who had led an earlier war powers resolution in April. Jayapal said she was in India attending to a health emergency involving her mother. "Had I been in Washington, D.C., I would have voted YES," she said in a statement, calling the conflict an "illegal war of choice" that had killed 13 US servicemembers and caused gas and grocery costs to "skyrocket."

For the Indian diaspora, the war's economic fallout has been impossible to ignore. The conflict, which began on February 28 with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, has effectively shut the Strait of Hormuz — a chokepoint that carried more than 40 percent of India's crude oil imports before the war. Oil prices touched $97 a barrel on Wednesday after Iranian drones struck Kuwait's airport. India, which imports 90 percent of the crude it consumes, has scrambled to find alternative sources, turning to Venezuela, whose acting president arrived in New Delhi on the same day as the vote.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio pushed back against the resolution in testimony before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, warning that Tehran would think the administration's "hands are going to be tied" and lose incentive to negotiate. Trump himself, in a podcast interview released Wednesday, suggested a deal with Iran could come as soon as this weekend. "If it happens, it could happen over the weekend," he told reporters without elaborating.

## What Comes Next

The resolution is largely symbolic for now. It must also pass the Senate to take effect, and even then, the administration has questioned whether war powers resolutions are constitutional. A veto is all but guaranteed.

But the politics are shifting. Republican lawmakers have also pushed back on Trump's "weaponisation" fund for political allies and criticised his appointment of Bill Pulte — a mortgage regulator with no national security experience — as acting director of national intelligence.

For Indian families watching fuel prices and flight disruptions, the vote is a signal that the war's domestic costs are becoming untenable even within the President's own party. Whether that signal reaches the Senate chamber remains the harder question.
author: Diaspora Desk
